heading: Questions we answer at the counter

items.question: How is a piece priced?
items.answer: Weight times the day’s rate for its karat gives the gold value. A making charge for the work is added, then 5% VAT. All three are itemised on the invoice so you can compare shops line by line.

items.question: How often does the gold rate change?
items.answer: The Dubai Jewellery Group publishes its suggested retail rate each morning and may update it during the day when the market moves. The boards in our branches and this website show the latest posted rate.

items.question: What does 916 on my jewellery mean?
items.answer: 916 is the fineness of 22-karat gold: 916 parts per thousand, or 91.6% pure. Every piece sold in the UAE must carry a hallmark, and Dubai Municipality’s Dubai Central Laboratory inspects jewellers to check it.

items.question: What do I need to bring to exchange old gold?
items.answer: Just the gold and your Emirates ID or passport. We test and weigh it in front of you and credit its full gold value, by weight at the day’s rate, against any new piece.

items.question: Do diamonds come with certificates?
items.answer: Every stone is instrument-tested in the shop before it is sold, and larger diamonds come with an independent laboratory grading report. Ask to watch the test.

items.question: Can tourists claim back VAT?
items.answer: Jewellery carries 5% VAT. Visitors may be able to reclaim it through the UAE’s Planet Tax Free scheme (minimum AED 250 per invoice, validated at the airport within 90 days). Ask in store whether your purchase qualifies.
